title: [CQ-M07i] Seat VM start and stop
description:
Slice of CQ-M07 (task-1a8f1d0e199046a289e94a5453d758b8); M07 DoD 5 (VM deleted on every exit path through the owned ledger). Design: mem:decision-cq-m07-verified-local-activation, decision 1. Depends on CQ-M07g (task-9076afab, seat owner) and CQ-M07h (task-eb783f59, cap); transitively on task-fd196d13's transport.

GATE: BACKLOG until task-fd196d13's transport design is ruled and CQ-M07g/h have plans; then move it to PLANNING.

Objective: the host side of one VM per seat. Provision the seat's owned VM once when a worker or QA seat starts, and delete it through the owned ledger when the seat stops, on every path.

Deliverable: new scripts/local-runner/agent-seat.mjs with startSeat and stopSeat, plus a CLI entry the wrappers call (subcommands seat-start and seat-stop; one JSON line out; fixed codes; exit codes documented in the module header; the planner picks the entry file and names it for CQ-M07m/n).
- startSeat: capacity admission (CQ-M07h) BEFORE any reserve or provider call; then provisionGuest (provision.mjs) into vm-control.mjs ownedLedgerDir(project) with the seat owner and this host's pinned client; R07 readiness; installAgents (pinned agent cache) and installToolchain (snapshot-transfer.mjs); then print the instance. Any failure after reserve deletes the VM with deleteOwned by its exact owned name; a failed delete keeps the record for cleanup (CQ-M07g).
- stopSeat: deleteOwned by exact owned name, idempotent; it never touches another record.
- Transport, keys and timeouts follow whatever task-fd196d13 lands.
- Add the module to `shipped` in scripts/tests/local-runner-bundle.test.mjs.

NOT in scope: running jobs (CQ-M07j); the wrappers (CQ-M07m/n).

Verification: in a git-archive snapshot (mem:gotcha-local-runner-tests recipe) with this task's files overlaid: env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" node --test <the new test file> scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-bundle.test.mjs
definitionOfDone: startSeat provisions exactly one owned VM with the seat owner and reports its instance; each refusal is a fixed code (fake-provider rows).
With the cap full, startSeat returns the capacity code before any ledger reserve or provider call (row).
A failure at any stage after reserve leaves no VM: deleteOwned runs with the exact owned name, and a failed delete keeps the record (table).
stopSeat deletes only the seat's VM and is idempotent (rows).
The named tests pass in a git-archive snapshot.
taskRails: No seat runs Multipass; tests use fakes, and the real-VM run is the human's or the governor's.

implementationPlan.description:
startSeat happy path and admission, in the new scripts/local-runner/agent-seat.mjs. Rail: no seat runs Multipass, every test uses fakes. Read mem:gotcha-local-runner-tests first (no forbidden-pattern literals; numstat counts).
The production composer to mirror is check-dispatch.mjs landedRunCheck plus check-lifecycle.mjs runCheckJob.
export startSeat(input, steps = {}).
- input is exactly { project, owner }. project is absolute with no control characters; owner passes validSeatOwner (CQ-M07g). Anything else is SEAT_INPUT_INVALID, before any read or step.
- steps holds the injectable defaults: provision = provisionGuest, toolchain = fetchNodeToolchain, installToolchain and installAgents (snapshot-transfer.mjs), remove = deleteOwned, count = countSeatVms, cap = hostAgentVmCap, admit = admitSeatVm (CQ-M07h, seat-capacity.mjs), probe = runnerProbe (vm-control.mjs), supervisor = reading new URL('./guest-supervisor.py', import.meta.url).
Order:
(1) platform = platformFor(process.platform), else SEAT_UNSUPPORTED_HOST. provider = { executable: platform.executable }; never a bare multipass.
(2) { root, ledger } = seatAdmissionFor(project). cacheDir = path.join(path.dirname(ownedLedgerDir(project)), 'images'), the check-dispatch convention.
(3) The own-record sweep (step 2).
(4) The capacity pre-check: (await count(root)).count >= cap() returns SEAT_CAPACITY_FULL, with no ledger reserve and no provider call. A count throw is SEAT_CAPACITY_UNKNOWN.
(5) Read the supervisor; failure is SEAT_SUPERVISOR_UNAVAILABLE.
(6) provision({ platform, ledger: wrapped, owner, cacheDir, supervisor, credential: randomBytes(32), provider }). The wrapped ledger is { ...ledger, reserve: async who => { const record = await admit({ root, ledger, owner: who }); run.record = record; return record; } }. provisionGuest reserves exactly once, after its prerequisites, so the cap is re-checked under CQ-M07h's host lock together with the write. A race lost there throws SEAT_CAPACITY_FULL with nothing reserved.
(7) Validate the result:
  - provisioned !== true: SEAT_PROVISION_UNAVAILABLE;
  - instance !== run.record.instance: SEAT_PROVISION_FAILED;
  - bootstrapReady !== true or failures non-empty: SEAT_GUEST_NOT_READY (R07 readiness already ran inside provisionGuest);
  - arch = image.source.arch, which must be in IMAGE_ARCHES: else SEAT_TOOLCHAIN_FAILED.
(8) toolchain({ arch, cacheDir }), then installToolchain({ name, toolchain, provider }), then installAgents({ name, arch, cacheDir, provider }).
(9) Resolve a frozen { ok: true, instance, executionReady: false }.
Codes: a thrown error whose code matches /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$/ passes through (native-smoke stableCode); anything else becomes the stage's fixed code (SEAT_PROVISION_FAILED, SEAT_TOOLCHAIN_FAILED, SEAT_AGENTS_FAILED). Never message text, a path or a key.
Tests in the new scripts/tests/local-runner-seat.test.mjs. Use a real CQ-M07g ledger under MOE_RUNNER_STATE_DIR set to a scratch dir, registering the t.after restore BEFORE mutating env (gotcha). The fake provision reserves through the wrapped ledger, moves the record to owned with ledger.update, and returns { provisioned: true, instance, bootstrapReady: true, failures: [], image: { source: { arch: 'x64' } } }.
- AS1 (DoD 1): ok with that instance. The ledger holds exactly one seat record, with this owner. The steps ran in order with the exact name. Refusals: a bad owner, a relative project and an extra key are SEAT_INPUT_INVALID with every step untouched; provisioned false is SEAT_PROVISION_UNAVAILABLE.
- AS2 (DoD 2): count >= cap gives SEAT_CAPACITY_FULL. admit, provision and every provider-touching step are never called, and the ledger stays empty.

implementationPlan.description:
Failure cleanup and the own-record sweep (agent-seat.mjs).
(a) Cleanup. Every failure once run.record is set ends with remove({ ledger, name: run.record.instance, owner, provider }) by that exact name. The real deleteOwned enforces the owner and purges the VM plus its guest-ssh key files only once the VM is verified absent.
  - 'deleted' gives vm 'deleted'.
  - 'not-launched' with a re-read phase of 'reserved' means it was reserved and never launched: ledger.retire(fresh record) (CQ-M07g), so the reservation stops counting toward the cap; vm 'retired'.
  - 'not-launched' in collision: the name is foreign, so leave it; vm 'none'.
  - A throw from remove or retire gives vm 'delete-failed'. The record is KEPT for CQ-M07g reconcile and cleanup; never retried in a loop, never forced.
  Resolve a frozen { ok: false, code, vm }, where code is the stage's code (the original failure, never the cleanup's). A failure before any reserve gives vm 'none'.
(b) The own-record sweep runs before the capacity pre-check, because a stale own record counts toward the cap. List the project ledger and pick seat records in reserved or a launched phase that are either:
  - exactly this owner (same workerId, runner and host), left by a seat-start that was killed after reserving; or
  - a previous incarnation of this seat: same workerId, a different runner, and probe(record) === false, meaning that runner is proven dead on this host and platform.
  Remove each through (a)'s path, passing the record's own { workerId, runner, host } as owner. Any failure refuses SEAT_PREVIOUS_VM_UNREMOVED: never provision a second VM while an earlier one may live. Every other record (another worker, an alive or unknown runner, attempt-owned, collision, deleted) is never touched. With no such record the sweep is a ledger read only, so AS2 still sees zero provider calls.
Tests:
- AS3 (DoD 3, table). Use real deleteOwned with a fake provider run (local-runner-vm-control.test.mjs fakeProvider style) and provider.keyDir set to a scratch dir. Fail once at each stage after reserve: provision throws after reserve and launch; bootstrapReady false; failures non-empty; toolchain fetch throws; installToolchain throws; installAgents throws. Each makes exactly one remove call with the captured name and owner and gives vm 'deleted'. Then:
  - a reserve followed by a throw before launch: vm 'retired' and the record file is gone;
  - a provider whose delete fails: vm 'delete-failed', and ledger.read(name) still returns the record;
  - each code is the stage's.
- AS5, the sweep:
  - an own leftover owned record is deleted before the new VM is provisioned, leaving exactly one live seat record;
  - a same-workerId record whose runner probe answers false is reclaimed;
  - one answering true or undefined, and another worker's record, are untouched;
  - a failing sweep delete gives SEAT_PREVIOUS_VM_UNREMOVED with no provision call.
implementationPlan.note:
Cleanup and the own-record sweep in agent-seat.mjs.

(a) removeVm(ledger, name, owner, s):
- remove (deleteOwned) by the exact name: 'deleted' gives 'deleted'.
- 'not-launched' re-reads the record: reserved is ledger.retire(fresh), giving 'retired'; any other phase (collision) gives 'none'.
- Any other answer, or any throw, propagates, and the record is kept.
- startSeat's catch: code = codeOf(error, run.stage), the original failure. With run.record set, the cleanup is removeVm(...).catch(() => 'delete-failed'): one call, never a loop.

(b) sweep() runs before the cap pre-check. It covers seat records in reserved, launching, owned, absent or failed with the same workerId, that are either:
- the exact owner (runner and host); or
- another runner with probe(record) === false.
Each is removed with ownerOf(record). Any failure is SEAT_PREVIOUS_VM_UNREMOVED.

Tests (TDD on existing code; RED proven by mutation):
- AS3, a 9-row table: provision throws, instance mismatch, bootstrapReady false, failures, bad arch, toolchain, installToolchain (opaque and coded TRANSFER_EXIT_FAILED), installAgents. Each has exactly one remove [w.reserved, SEAT], a record marked deleted, and the VM gone. Also: reserve then throw gives retired; a stuck delete gives delete-failed with the record kept and owned.
- AS5: own owned, own reserved and a dead incarnation are swept. Live, unprovable, another worker's dead and this runner on another host are kept. A stuck own record gives SEAT_PREVIOUS_VM_UNREMOVED with only remove steps run.

Mutation sweep (/tmp/m07i-mut/run.mjs, scratch copies only): 26 of 26 mutants KILLED after adding the M18 collision row and the M19 unexpected-remove row. The baseline is green.

Size: 182 + 211 + 4 + 2 = 399 of 400.

stopSeat(input, steps):
- input is exactly {project, owner, instance}, where instance passes isOwnedInstanceName; else SEAT_INPUT_INVALID.
- kit() pins the provider executable.
- An absent record file (lstat ENOENT on ownedLedgerDir(project)/<instance>.json) gives 'gone' with no provider call.
- Otherwise removeVm via createLedger(dir) by that exact name and owner: deleted, retired or none (collision).
- LIFECYCLE_NOT_OWNER passes through with vm 'none'. Every other failure is SEAT_STOP_FAILED with vm 'delete-failed', and the record is kept.
- It never lists or sweeps.

AS4 rows:
- A is deleted, and every provider call names A.
- A second stop of A gives 'deleted' with zero provider calls.
- B (another worker) with SEAT's owner gives LIFECYCLE_NOT_OWNER; B's bytes and the call count are unchanged.
- Reserved C gives 'retired', then 'gone'.
- Stuck D gives SEAT_STOP_FAILED with the record kept and owned.
- A bad instance gives SEAT_INPUT_INVALID.
- A collision E gives ok with vm 'none' and stays collision.
- An unexpected remove answer gives SEAT_STOP_FAILED.

Mutants M08 (NOT_OWNER mapped away), M18, M19 and M20 (lstat gone path) are all KILLED by AS4.

implementationPlan.note: Adversarial self-review found one real problem and fixed it. In startSeat's catch, codeOf(error, run.stage) ran BEFORE the cleanup. If provision reserved a VM and then threw an error whose `code` getter itself throws, the throw escaped the catch, the reserved VM was never deleted, and runAgentSeat could only report SEAT_FAILED. Fix: cleanup first, code second. The vm is removeVm(...).catch(() => 'delete-failed') when a record was reserved, else 'none', and only then failed(codeOf(error, run.stage), vm). The cleanup cannot be skipped, and the reported code is always the original failure's, never the cleanup's. I changed AS6's trap row to match: provision now reserves before throwing the trapped error. Before the fix it was RED: ledger phases ['deleted','reserved']. After the fix it is GREEN, with the phases exactly ['deleted'] and the exact 6 output lines. Mutation sweep (/tmp/m07i-mut, outside the checkout): 28 of 28 mutants KILLED. The M00 baseline is green. The killed mutants include M06 (no cleanup in the catch) and M28 (code read before cleanup). Since the bytes changed, I re-ran step 5's exact gate on a fresh git-archive snapshot at HEAD 830e8399 with the 4 overlays: exit 0, tests 407, pass 406, fail 0, skipped 1 (the macOS native smoke that was already skipped). Size is 398 against the 400 cap: agent-seat.mjs +181, local-runner-seat.test.mjs +211, bundle test +2/-2, ci.yml +1/-1. No forbidden patterns. Residuals I considered and documented, not fixed: (1) two concurrent seat-starts for the same owner are not serialized. The header says so, and wrappers launch seats one at a time. (2) In stopSeat, a concurrent retire between the lstat and the read gives SEAT_STOP_FAILED, and a retry then answers 'gone'. (3) The sweep can call the provider before the cap pre-check, by design. With no leftover records it only reads the ledger. (4) Tests never run Multipass, per the rail; the real-VM run is for the human or the governor. Out of scope: I filed bug task-7d7d608264164f98a46a69910284f98c. waitForGuestReady (guest-readiness.mjs:252) compares only taskId/attemptId/generation, so any owner passes the check on a seat record. It matters for CQ-M07m/n.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: scripts/local-runner/agent-seat.mjs provides startSeat, stopSeat and a CLI (seat-start/seat-stop, one JSON line, exit 0/1/2/75). startSeat first reclaims this seat's own leftover or proven-dead previous-incarnation VM. It then provisions one seat-owned VM through provisionGuest, whose single reserve runs under CQ-M07h's locked admission, verifies R07 readiness and installs the pinned toolchain and agents. Any failure after reserve removes that exact VM, or retires a never-launched reservation; a failed delete keeps the record. stopSeat deletes only the named instance of this owner, idempotently.
invariants: Exactly one live seat VM per owner after a successful startSeat; the capacity check and reserve are atomic under the host lock.
Every removal goes through deleteOwned (or ledger.retire for a reserved record) by an exact owned name; a failed delete never loses the record.
No output carries a path, key, credential or stderr; executionReady is always false.
Tests never run multipass and never signal a process.
compatibility: provisionGuest, deleteOwned, installAgents and installToolchain are used unchanged; the bundle test gains a shipped entry and CI one test file.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. Admitting (lock plus reserve) before provisionGuest and handing it a pre-reserved record: rejected. A prerequisite failure would strand a reservation, and the slot would be held during the ~600 MB image download. Instead an unlocked pre-check refuses early, and the locked admission runs at provisionGuest's own reserve.
2. Reclaiming a previous incarnation only through vm-control cleanup: rejected. Cleanup holds it as 'seat-registered' while the new incarnation is registered (CQ-M07g handoff). startSeat reclaims it on the runner-dead proof instead.
3. CLI subcommands in cli.mjs: rejected. cli.mjs is in `required`; a direct entry like vm-control.mjs is self-contained.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- check-lifecycle.mjs runCheckJob shows the capture-reservation ledger wrapper and the finally-delete pattern; vm 'not-launched' leaves a reserved record.
- provisionGuest writes the guest-ssh transport files after provisionOwned.
- invoker defaults to a bare 'multipass', so always pass the pinned executable.
- CI lists local-runner test files explicitly.
planningNotes.risks:
